title: Tunnels that wander, and the sky is out of the cave
question: Three things since the last card. The tunnels were straight because a shortest path on a grid is a straight line -- so the roughness is now in the cost field itself and the route bends because going round is genuinely cheaper, and the bore's width rides a slow wobble instead of being one radius. The sky you saw leaking in was the renderer, not a hole: a shaft has no ground above it, so daylight was spending none of its budget coming down one and arriving in the chamber with the lot intact; it is now measured against the ground *around* the column. And there are two new smaller size bands, so a system has rooms a few gnome-heights across as well as halls. Do the passages read as natural now, and is there enough in the middle of the size range?
